 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Economic and Business Relationship Risks </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Local media rights are a significant revenue stream for our business. Decreases in local media rights revenue have had an adverse effect on our business
and results of operations, and the effect of future reductions, including from a bankruptcy of MSG Networks, could be material. </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Local media rights represent a significant revenue stream for the Company. In Fiscal Year 2026, we recorded $35.3&nbsp;million of local media
rights revenues, which represented 10% of our total revenues in Fiscal Year 2026, compared to $39.1 million in Fiscal Year 2025, which represented 12% of our total revenues. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Business conditions impacting our broadcasting partner, MSG Networks, including the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">work-out</FONT> of MSG
Networks (as discussed below) and/or actions by the NHL, have in the past adversely affected and could in the future materially adversely affect the revenue that can be derived from these media rights. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In October 2015, the Rangers entered into a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">20-year</FONT> local telecast rights agreement with MSG Networks,
a regional sports network and wholly-owned subsidiary of Sphere Entertainment to provide MSG Networks with exclusive local linear and digital rights to home and away games of the Rangers, as well as other team-related programming. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In recent years, regional sports networks, including MSG Networks, have experienced significant financial difficulties. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Networks was not able to refinance its credit facilities prior to their maturity in October 2024. After a series of forbearances from its
lenders, on June&nbsp;27, 2025, MSG Networks restructured its indebtedness, with MSG Networks&#8217; lenders writing off approximately $510&nbsp;million of indebtedness. As part of MSG Networks&#8217; debt restructuring process, the local telecast
rights agreement between MSG Networks and the Rangers was amended to effect a fee reduction of 18%, effective as of January&nbsp;1, 2025, with no annual rights fee escalator. In addition, the term of the local telecast rights agreement was reduced
to end after the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2028-29</FONT> season. In connection with the expiration of the rights agreement, MSG Networks has the right to make a firm offer for an additional term of not less than 3 seasons and the right to
match a third party offer that provides for rights fees that are not at least 110% of the rights fees for the first 3 years of the term specified in the firm offer. As a result of the amendment and other terms of the local telecast rights agreement,
media rights fees for the Rangers were approximately $2.2&nbsp;million lower for Fiscal Year 2025 compared to the prior fiscal year, and approximately $3.8&nbsp;million lower for Fiscal Year 2026, compared to Fiscal Year 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although MSG Networks completed the workout of its indebtedness on June&nbsp;27, 2025, MSG Networks could in the future default on its
obligations under the local telecast rights agreement or seek bankruptcy protection, including as a result of loss of carriage of its programming by its distributors through <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-renewal</FONT> of affiliation
agreements, loss of subscribers or transition of MSG Networks to a more limited tier of service. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If MSG Networks were to default on its
local telecast rights agreement with us or discharge its local telecast rights agreement with us as part of a bankruptcy proceeding or otherwise, or if we do not renew the agreement upon its expiration, we would lose a significant recurring revenue
stream, and would also lose the exposure provided by the MSG Networks broadcasting related to the Rangers, any of which could have a material negative effect on our business and results of operations. Although we would pursue alternative sources of
distribution for home and away games of the Rangers, as well as other team-related programming, there can be no assurances as to the timing or success of such alternative sources of distribution, all of which would be subject to the approval of the
NHL. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Our business has been adversely impacted and may, in the future, be materially adversely impacted by an economic downturn, recession,
financial instability or inflation. </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our business depends upon the ability and willingness of consumers and businesses to purchase
tickets (including season tickets) to our games, license suites at The Garden, spend on food and beverages and </P>

Entertainment. Certain government officials and special interest groups have in the past used, and may in the future use, the renewal process for the zoning special permit to pressure MSG Entertainment to make financial contributions or other

definitive documentation and other agreements. There can be no assurance regarding the future renewal of the permit or the terms thereof, or regarding the timing, scope, terms or completion of any Penn Station redevelopment or related arrangements,

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Our business is subject to seasonal fluctuations and our operating results and cash flows can vary substantially from period to period. </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our revenues and expenses have been seasonal and we expect they will continue to be seasonal. Due to the NHL playing season, revenues from our

connection with one of our games or an event hosted by MSG Entertainment at The Garden could also reduce attendance at our other games and may have a negative impact on our revenue and results of operations. Under the Arena License Agreement, MSG
Entertainment and the Company have reciprocal indemnity obligations to each other in connection with their respective acts or omissions in or about The Garden during the home games of the Rangers. We, and the NHL maintain insurance policies that
provide coverage for incidents in the ordinary course of business, but there can be no assurance that such indemnities or insurance will be adequate at all times and in all circumstances. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">From time to time, the Company, its subsidiaries and/or its affiliates are involved in various legal proceedings, including proceedings or
lawsuits brought by governmental agencies, stockholders, customers, employees, other private parties and other stakeholders. The outcome of litigation is inherently unpredictable and, regardless of the merits of the claims, litigation may be
expensive, time-consuming, disruptive to our operations and distracting to management. In addition, publicity from these matters could negatively impact our business or reputation, regardless of the accuracy of such publicity. As a result, we may
incur liability from litigation (including in connection with settling such litigation) which could be material and for which we may not have available or adequate insurance coverage or be subject to other forms of
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-monetary</FONT> relief which may adversely affect the Company. The liabilities and any defense costs we incur in connection with any such litigation could have an adverse effect on our business and results of
operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Risks Related to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-off</FONT> Transaction </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Because there has not been any public market for our common stock, the market price and trading volume of our common stock may be volatile and you may
not be able to resell your shares at or above the initial market price of our stock following the Distribution. </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Prior to the
Distribution, there will have been no regular way trading market for our common stock. We cannot predict the extent to which investors&#8217; interest will lead to a liquid trading market or whether the market price of our common stock will be
volatile. The market price of our common stock could fluctuate significantly for many reasons, including in response to the risk factors listed in this information statement or for reasons unrelated to our specific performance, such as reports by
industry analysts, investor perceptions or negative developments for our customers, competitors or suppliers, as well as general economic and industry conditions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>The combined post-Distribution value of MSG Sports and Spinco shares may not equal or exceed the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-distribution</FONT> value of MSG Sports shares. </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">After the Distribution, MSG Sports
Class&nbsp;A Common Stock will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE. We cannot assure you that the combined trading prices of MSG Sports Class&nbsp;A Common Stock and Spinco Class&nbsp;A Common Stock after the Distribution, as adjusted for
any changes in the combined capitalization of these companies, will be equal to or greater than the trading price of MSG Sports Class&nbsp;A Common Stock prior to the Distribution. Until the market has fully evaluated the business of MSG Sports
without the business of Spinco, the price at which MSG Sports Class&nbsp;A Common Stock trades may fluctuate significantly. Similarly, until the market has fully evaluated the business of Spinco, the price at which shares of Spinco Class&nbsp;A
Common Stock trade may fluctuate significantly. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports expects to obtain an opinion from Sullivan&nbsp;&amp; Cromwell LLP substantially to the effect that, among other things, the

income tax consequences of the Distribution. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If the Distribution does not qualify for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-free</FONT>
treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes, then, in general, MSG Sports would recognize taxable gain in an amount equal to the excess of the fair market value of our common stock distributed in the Distribution over MSG Sports&#8217; tax basis
therein (i.e., as if it had sold such common stock in a taxable sale for its fair market value). In addition, the receipt by MSG Sports stockholders of common stock of our Company would be a taxable distribution, and each U.S. holder that receives
our common stock in the Distribution would be treated as if the U.S. holder had received a distribution equal to the fair market value of our common stock that was distributed to it, which generally would be treated first as a taxable dividend to
the extent of such holder&#8217;s pro rata share of MSG Sports&#8217; earnings and profits, then as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-taxable</FONT> return of capital to the extent of the&nbsp;holder&#8217;s tax basis in its MSG Sports common
stock, and thereafter as capital gain with respect to any remaining value. It is expected that the amount of any such taxes to MSG Sports stockholders and MSG Sports would be substantial. See &#8220;The Distribution&nbsp;&#8212; Material U.S.

of our internal control over financial reporting or our auditors identify material weaknesses in our internal controls, investor confidence in our financial results may weaken, and our stock price may suffer. </P>

a fiscal year; (b)&nbsp;issue more than $1&nbsp;billion of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-convertible</FONT> debt over a three-year period; or (c)&nbsp;become a &#8220;large accelerated filer&#8221; as defined in Rule <FONT

of such holders of our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock (other than the Excluded Trusts) to be cast as a block with respect to all matters to be voted on by such holders of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock owned by Excluded Trusts will on all matters be voted on in accordance with the determination of the
Excluded Trusts holding a majority of the Class&nbsp;B Common Stock held by all Excluded Trusts, except in the case of a vote on a going-private transaction or a change in control transaction, in which case a vote of trusts holding <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-thirds</FONT> of the Class&nbsp;B Common Stock owned by Excluded Trusts is required. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under the
Stockholders Agreement, the shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock owned by members of the Dolan Family Group (other than the Excluded Trusts) are to be voted on all matters in accordance with the determination of the Dolan Family Committee. The
&#8220;Dolan Family Committee&#8221; will consist of James L. Dolan, Patrick F. Dolan, Kathleen M. Dolan, Marianne Dolan Weber and Deborah A. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Dolan-Sweeney.</FONT> The Dolan Family Committee generally acts by
majority vote, except that approval of a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">going-private</FONT> transaction must be approved by a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-thirds</FONT> vote and approval of a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">change-in-control</FONT></FONT> transaction must be approved by not less than all but one vote. The voting members of the Dolan Family Committee will be James&nbsp;L. Dolan, Kathleen M.&nbsp;Dolan, Marianne Dolan Weber and
Deborah A. Dolan-Sweeney, with each member having one vote other than James L. Dolan, who will have two votes. Because James L. Dolan will have two votes, he will have the ability to block Dolan Family Committee approval of any Company change in
control transaction. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Dolan Family Group, by virtue of their stock ownership, have the ability to determine all matters requiring
approval by stockholders (other than the election of the Class A Directors and any matters requiring a separate vote by the holders of the Class A Common Stock) and are able collectively to control stockholder decisions on matters on which holders
of our Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock vote together as a single class (including, but not limited to, a change-in-control), and to elect up to 75% of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. Certain Dolan family trusts (the
&#8220;Excluded Trusts&#8221;) will collectively own the majority of the outstanding shares of the Company&#8217;s Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. These matters could include the amendment of some provisions of our amended and restated articles of
incorporation. The Company&#8217;s capital structure and the disparate voting rights of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock may have anti-takeover effects, including that the Dolan Family Group is able to prevent a
change in control of the Company or other fundamental corporate transaction that our stockholders might consider in their best interest. No person interested in acquiring us would be able to do so without obtaining the consent of the Dolan Family
Group, which includes the Excluded Trusts. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the affirmative vote or consent of the holders of at least 66&nbsp;2/3% of the

involving or affecting each company. For example, there will be the potential for a conflict of interest when we on the one hand, and MSG Entertainment, MSG Sports, Sphere Entertainment and/or AMC Global Media and their respective subsidiaries and
successors on the other hand, look at certain acquisitions and other corporate opportunities that may be suitable for more than one of the companies. Also, conflicts may arise if there are issues or disputes under the commercial arrangements that
will exist between an Other Entity and us. In addition, after the Distribution, certain of our directors and officers will continue to own stock and/or stock options or other equity awards of an Other Entity. These ownership interests could create
actual, apparent or potential conflicts of interest when these individuals are faced with decisions that could have different implications for our Company and an Other Entity. See &#8220;Certain Relationships and Related Party
Transactions&nbsp;&#8212; Certain Relationships and Potential Conflicts of Interest&#8221; for a discussion of certain procedures we will institute to help ameliorate such potential conflicts that may arise. </P>

District Court of Clark County, Nevada shall, to the fullest extent permitted bylaw, be the exclusive forum for substantially all disputes between us and our stockholders, which could limit our stockholders&#8217; ability to obtain a judicial forum
it finds favorable for disputes with us or our directors, officers or controlling stockholders. </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Nevada Revised Statutes allow
Nevada corporations to include a provision in their articles of incorporation or bylaws that requires, to the extent not inconsistent with any applicable federal laws, internal actions be brought solely or exclusively in courts specified therein,
and those specified courts must include at least one court in the State of Nevada. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As permitted by those statutes, our amended and
restated bylaws will provide that the Eighth Judicial District Court of Clark County, Nevada shall, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for state law claims with respect to any actions, suits or proceedings,
whether civil, administrative or investigative, that is an internal action (as defined in Nevada Revised Statutes 78.046), as to which the Nevada Revised Statutes confer jurisdiction on the district court of the State of Nevada, or asserting a claim
governed by the internal affairs doctrine. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our amended and restated bylaws will further provide that, to the fullest extent permitted by
law, and unless the Company consents in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United&nbsp;States shall be the sole and exclusive forum for any claim arising under the Securities Act. However, our
amended and restated bylaws will also provide that if this provision, or the application of this provision to any person or any circumstance is illegal, invalid or unenforceable, the Eighth Judicial District Court of Clark County, Nevada shall be
the sole and exclusive state court forum for any claim arising under the Securities Act or any rule or regulation promulgated thereunder (in each case, as amended from time to time). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Notwithstanding the foregoing, our exclusive forum provision will not apply to suits brought to enforce any liability, obligation or duty
created by the Exchange Act or any rule or regulation promulgated thereunder (in each case, as amended from time to time) or any other claim for which the federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction to the extent such application would be contrary to
law. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Any person purchasing or otherwise acquiring any interest in shares of capital stock of the Company shall be deemed to have notice
of and consented to our exclusive forum provision. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This exclusive forum provision may limit a stockholder&#8217;s ability to bring a
claim in a judicial forum that it finds favorable for disputes with us or our directors, officers or controlling stockholders, which may discourage lawsuits against us and our directors, officers and controlling stockholders. If a stockholder of the
Company may nevertheless seek to bring a claim in a venue other than the Eighth Judicial District Court of Clark County, Nevada as designated in the exclusive forum provision of our bylaws, we would expect to vigorously assert the validity and
enforceability of the exclusive forum provision in our bylaws. This may require significant additional costs associated with resolving actions in other jurisdictions and there can be no assurance that the exclusive forum provision will be enforced
by a court in those other jurisdictions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">There is uncertainty as to whether a court will enforce an exclusive forum selection provision
such as ours. If a court were to find the exclusive forum provision in our bylaws to be inapplicable or unenforceable in an action, we may incur further significant additional costs associated with resolving the dispute in other jurisdictions, all
of which could harm our business. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc127770_6"></A>THE DISTRIBUTION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>General </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports will distribute all
of our outstanding stock to the holders of MSG Sports Class&nbsp;A Common Stock and Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. We refer to this distribution of securities as the &#8220;Distribution,&#8221; the Class&nbsp;A Common Stock distributed as the
&#8220;Distributed Class&nbsp;A Common Stock,&#8221; the Class&nbsp;B Common Stock distributed as the &#8220;Distributed Class&nbsp;B Common Stock&#8221; (and, together with the Distributed Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, the &#8220;Distributed Common
Stock&#8221;). The Distributed Common Stock will include 100% of the outstanding shares of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock (the holders of which will have the right to collectively elect at least 25% of our Board of Directors, rounded up to the nearest
whole number of directors) and 100% of the outstanding shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock (the holders of which will have the right to collectively elect up to the remaining 75% of our Board of Directors). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the Distribution, each holder of MSG Sports common stock will receive a distribution of one share of our common stock for every two shares
of MSG Sports common stock held as of the close of business, New York City time, on October 20, 2026, which will be the record date. Immediately following the Distribution, owners of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock (the &#8220;Class&nbsp;A Common
Stockholders&#8221;) of MSG Sports will own 100% of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, and owners of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock (the &#8220;Class&nbsp;B Common Stockholders &#8220;) of MSG Sports will own 100% of our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Manner of Effecting the Distribution </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The general terms and conditions relating to the Distribution will be set forth in the Distribution Agreement between us and MSG Sports. Under
the Distribution Agreement, the Distribution will be effective at 11:59&nbsp;p.m., New&nbsp;York City time, on October 26, 2026. For most MSG Sports stockholders who own MSG Sports common stock in registered form on the record date, our transfer and
distribution agent will credit their shares of our common stock to book entry accounts established to hold these shares. Our transfer and distribution agent will send these stockholders a statement reflecting their ownership of our common stock.
Book entry refers to a method of recording stock ownership in our records in which no physical certificates are used. For stockholders who own MSG Sports common stock through a broker or other nominee, their shares of our common stock will be
credited to these stockholders&#8217; accounts by the broker or other nominee. As further discussed below, fractional shares will not be distributed. Following the Distribution, stockholders whose shares are held in book entry form may request that
their shares of our common stock be transferred to a brokerage or other account at any time, as well as delivery of physical stock certificates for their shares, in each case without charge. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG SPORTS STOCKHOLDERS WILL NOT BE REQUIRED TO PAY FOR SHARES&nbsp;OF OUR COMMON STOCK RECEIVED IN THE DISTRIBUTION, OR TO SURRENDER OR
EXCHANGE SHARES&nbsp;OF MSG SPORTS COMMON STOCK IN ORDER TO RECEIVE OUR COMMON STOCK, OR TO TAKE ANY OTHER ACTION IN CONNECTION WITH THE DISTRIBUTION. NO VOTE OF MSG SPORTS STOCKHOLDERS IS REQUIRED OR SOUGHT IN CONNECTION WITH THE DISTRIBUTION, AND
MSG SPORTS STOCKHOLDERS HAVE NO APPRAISAL RIGHTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE DISTRIBUTION. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Fractional shares of our common stock will not be
issued to MSG Sports stockholders as part of the Distribution or credited to book entry accounts. In lieu of receiving fractional shares, each holder of MSG Sports common stock who would otherwise be entitled to receive a fractional share of our
common stock will receive cash for the fractional interest, which generally will be taxable to such holder. An explanation of the tax consequences of the Distribution can be found below in the subsection captioned &#8220;&#8212;&nbsp;Material U.S.
Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Distribution.&#8221; The transfer and distribution agent will, as soon as practicable after the Distribution Date, aggregate fractional shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock into whole shares and sell them in
the open market at the prevailing market prices and distribute the aggregate proceeds, net of brokerage </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">43 </P>

fees, ratably to stockholders otherwise entitled to fractional interests in our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock. Similarly, fractional shares of our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock will be aggregated,
converted to Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, and sold in the public market by the transfer and distribution agent. The amount of such payments will depend on the prices at which the aggregated fractional shares are sold by the transfer and distribution
agent in the open market shortly after the Distribution Date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See &#8220;Executive Compensation&nbsp;&#8212; Treatment of Outstanding
Awards,&#8221; for a discussion of how outstanding MSG Sports options, restricted stock units and performance stock units will be affected by the Distribution. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In order to be entitled to receive shares of our common stock in the Distribution, MSG Sports stockholders must be&nbsp;stockholders of record
of MSG Sports common stock at the close of business, New&nbsp;York City time, on the record date, October 20, 2026. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Reasons for the Distribution
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors has determined that separation of our business from MSG Sports&#8217; other business is in the
best interests of MSG Sports and its stockholders. The potential benefits considered by MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors in making the determination to consummate the Distribution included the following: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">to provide each of MSG Sports and the Company with increased flexibility to fully pursue and fund its business
plan, including the ability to raise capital at each entity separately. This increased financial flexibility reflects the belief that investors in a company with the mix of assets that each of MSG Sports and the Company will own following the
Distribution will be more receptive to strategic initiatives that MSG Sports and the Company may respectively pursue; and </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">to increase the aggregate value of the stock of MSG Sports and the Company above the value that the stock of MSG
Sports would have had if it had continued to represent an interest in both the businesses of MSG Sports and the Company, so as to: (i)&nbsp;allow each company to use its stock to pursue and achieve strategic objectives, including accessing capital
on more attractive terms, evaluating and effectuating acquisitions and investments, and increasing the long-term attractiveness of equity compensation programs in a significantly more efficient and effective manner with significantly less dilution
to existing stockholders; and (ii)&nbsp;allow each company to offer a more focused investment profile to investors. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG
Sports&#8217; board of directors also considered several factors that might have a negative effect on MSG Sports as a result of the Distribution. MSG Sports common stock may come under initial selling pressure as certain MSG Sports stockholders sell
their shares because they are not interested in holding an investment in MSG Sport&#8217;s remaining business. Moreover, certain factors, such as a lack of comparable public companies, may limit investors&#8217; ability to appropriately value MSG
Sports common stock. In addition, the Distribution would separate from MSG Sports the business and assets of the Company, which represent significant value. Because the Company will no longer be part of MSG Sports, the Distribution will also affect
the terms upon which MSG Sports can pursue cross-company business transactions and initiatives with the Company. Finally, following the Distribution, MSG Sports and its remaining business will need to absorb certain corporate and administrative
costs previously allocated to its New York Rangers business. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors considered certain aspects of the
Distribution that may be adverse to the Company, including the impacts of the Company&#8217;s net loss for Fiscal Years 2025 and 2026. The Company&#8217;s common stock may come under initial selling pressure as certain MSG Sports stockholders sell
their shares in the Company because they are not interested in holding an investment in the Company&#8217;s business. Moreover, certain factors, such as a lack of comparable public companies, may limit investors&#8217; ability to appropriately value
the Company&#8217;s common stock. Because the Company will no longer be part of MSG Sports, the Distribution will also affect the terms upon which the Company can pursue <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">cross-company</FONT> business transactions and
initiatives with MSG Sports&#8217; other business. In addition, after the Distribution, the Company&#8217;s results, which reflected a net </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">44 </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><U>Our Business </U></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Our Sports Franchises </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>New York Rangers </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Rangers
hockey club is one of the NHL&#8217;s &#8220;Original Six&#8221; franchises and celebrated its centennial during the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2025-26</FONT> season. As a storied franchise and one of the league&#8217;s marquee teams, the
Rangers have won four Stanley Cup Championships and have a loyal and enthusiastic fan base. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Hartford Wolf Pack </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Hartford Wolf Pack, a minor-league hockey team in the AHL, is the top affiliate team for the Rangers. The Rangers send draft picks,
prospects and other players to the Hartford Wolf Pack to compete, gain valuable ice time and develop. The Rangers can call up players from Hartford to their own roster during the regular season when needed. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Arena License Agreement </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Garden, also
known as The World&#8217;s Most Famous Arena, is the home for the Rangers pursuant to the Arena License Agreement with MSG Entertainment. The Arena License Agreement provides revenue opportunities through the sharing of certain suites and clubs,
sponsorship and signage, food and beverage, merchandise and sales arrangements with MSG Entertainment. The Arena License Agreement has a term of 35&nbsp;years and expires in June 2055. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company owns the Madison Square Garden Training Center in Greenburgh, NY, which is used by the Rangers as well as the Knicks (which the

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>The Role of the NHL in Our Operations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As
a franchise in a professional sports league, the Rangers are a member of the NHL and, as such, are subject to certain rules, regulations and limitations on the control and management of their affairs. The NHL Constitution, under which the NHL is
operated, together with the CBA that the NHL has signed with its players&#8217; association, contains numerous provisions that, as a practical matter, could impact the manner in which we operate our business. In addition, under the NHL constitution,
the commissioner of the NHL, either acting alone or with the consent of a majority (or, in some cases, a supermajority) of the other NHL teams, may be empowered in certain circumstances to take certain actions believed to be in the best interests of
the league, whether or not such actions would benefit the Rangers and whether or not we consent or object to those actions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The NHL has a
degree of control exercisable under certain circumstances over the length and format of the playing season, including, for example, preseason and playoff schedules; the number of games in a playing season; the operating territories of the member
teams; local, national and international media and other licensing rights; admission of new members and changes in ownership; franchise relocations; indebtedness affecting the franchises and their affiliates; and labor relations with the
players&#8217; associations, including collective bargaining, free agency, and rules applicable to player transactions and revenue sharing. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Media

agreements with MSG Networks covering the local telecast and radio rights for the Rangers. The local telecast agreement has a remaining term of approximately three years. </P>

hockey clinics, summer camps, a girls hockey league, equipment donations and other &#8216;learn to play&#8217; initiatives in the community. In Fiscal Year 2025, Jr. Rangers programming extended across more than 1,350 individual sessions and 50
locations. The Company is also dedicated to affecting positive change through other social impact and cause-related initiatives including philanthropic food and other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-kind</FONT> donations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Garden of Dreams Foundation </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The

skills opportunities, mentoring programs and memorable </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our business operates in a market in which numerous sports and entertainment opportunities are available. In addition to the NHL team that we

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a result of the large number of options available, we face strong competition for the New
York area sports fan base. We must compete with these other sporting events in varying respects and degrees, including on the basis of the quality and success of the teams we field, our ability to provide an entertaining environment at our games and
the prices we charge. In addition, for fans who prefer the unique experience of NHL hockey, we must compete with the Islanders and Devils as well as, in varying respects and degrees, with other NHL hockey teams. We also compete to varying degrees
with the other New York metropolitan area sports teams, the NHL itself, and other productions and live entertainment events for advertising and sponsorship dollars. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The amount of revenue we earn is influenced by many factors, including the popularity and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT>
performance of the Rangers and general economic and health and safety conditions. In particular, when the Rangers have strong <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT> performance, we benefit from increased demand for tickets and premium
hospitality, potentially greater food, beverage and merchandise sales from increased attendance and increased sponsorship opportunities. When the Rangers qualify for the playoffs, we also benefit from the attendance and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-game</FONT> spending at the playoff games. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-to-year</FONT></FONT> impact of team performance is somewhat moderated by the fact that a significant
portion of our revenue derives from media rights fees, suite rental fees and sponsorship and signage revenue, all of which are generally contracted on a multi-year basis. Nevertheless, the long-term performance of our business is tied to the success
and popularity of the Rangers. In addition, due to the NHL playing seasons, revenues from our business are typically concentrated in the second and third quarters of each fiscal year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See &#8220;Risk Factors &#8212; Risks Related to our Business &#8212; <I>Our business faces intense and wide-ranging competition, which may
have a material negative effect on our business and results of operations&#8221; and &#8220;&#8212; Our business is substantially dependent on the continued popularity and/or competitive success of the Rangers, including the significant additional
revenue generated by the Rangers advancing in the playoffs, which cannot be assured.&#8221; </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Human Capital Resources </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We believe the strength of our workforce is one of the significant contributors to our success. Our key human capital management objectives are
to invest in and support our employees in order to attract, develop and retain a high performing and diverse workforce. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Talent </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of June 30, 2026, we had 144 full-time union and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-union</FONT> employees and three part-time union and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-union</FONT> employees. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We are committed to fostering a strong, inclusive workplace community where all

STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-free</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">spin-off</FONT> of the New York Rangers business from the New York Knicks business of MSG Sports, and on May&nbsp;12, 2026, the MSG Sports board of directors approved the
filing of a Form 10 registration statement and amendments thereto. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSGS Spinco, Inc. was incorporated in the state of Nevada on
April&nbsp;28, 2026 to be the company to hold the New York Rangers business of MSG Sports. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">spin-off</FONT> is expected to be completed through a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-free</FONT> pro rata
distribution of 100% of the common stock of the Company to MSG Sports stockholders (the &#8220;Distribution&#8221;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Completion of the

SEC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The combined financial statements of the Company were prepared on a standalone basis and derived from the consolidated financial

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Revenue Sources </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We earn revenue from several primary sources: ticket sales and a portion of suite rental fees at The Garden, our share of distributions from
NHL league-wide national and international media contracts and other league-wide revenue sources, sponsorships and signage, food and beverage sales at The Garden and merchandising<I>. </I>We also earn fees from MSG Networks for the local media
rights to telecast the games of the Rangers<I>. </I>The amount of revenue we earn is influenced by many factors, including the popularity and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT> performance of the Rangers (particularly the ability of the
Rangers to reach and advance in the NHL playoffs) and general economic and health and safety conditions. In particular, when the Rangers have strong <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT> performance, we benefit from increased demand for
tickets and premium hospitality, potentially greater food, beverage and merchandise sales from increased attendance and increased sponsorship opportunities. When the Rangers qualify for the playoffs, we also benefit from the attendance and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-game</FONT> spending at the playoff games. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-to-year</FONT></FONT> impact of team performance is somewhat moderated by the fact that a significant
portion of our revenue derives from media rights fees, suite rental fees and sponsorship and signage revenue, all of which are generally contracted on a multi-year basis. Nevertheless, the long-term performance of our business is tied to the success
and popularity of the Rangers. In addition, due to the NHL playing season, revenues from our business are typically concentrated in the second and third quarters of each fiscal year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Ticket Sales and Facility and Ticketing Fees </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Ticket sales have historically constituted our largest single source of revenue. Tickets to Rangers home games are sold through season tickets
(full and partial plans), which are typically held by long-term season ticket members, through group sales, and through single-game tickets, which are purchased by fans either individually or in multi-game packages. We generally review and set the
price of our tickets before the start of the Rangers season. However, we dynamically price our individual tickets based on opponent, seat location, day of the week and other factors. We do not earn revenue from ticket sales for games played by the
Rangers at their opponents&#8217; arenas. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We also earn revenue in the form of certain fees added to ticket prices, which currently
include a facility fee the Company charges on tickets it sells to Rangers games, except for season tickets. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Media Rights </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We earn revenue from the licensing of media rights for Rangers home and away games and also through the receipt of our share of fees paid for
league-wide media rights, which are awarded under contracts negotiated and administered by the NHL. Fees paid by telecasters under these arrangements are pooled by the NHL and then generally shared equally among all NHL teams. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company and MSG Networks are parties to a local telecast rights agreement covering the local telecast rights for the Rangers. On
June&nbsp;27, 2025, the Rangers and MSG Networks entered into an amendment with respect to the local telecast rights agreement. See &#8220;&#8212; Factors Affecting Operating Results &#8212; Amendments to Local Telecast Rights Agreement&#8221; for
more information. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Suites and Clubs </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We earn revenue through the sale of suite and premium club licenses at The Garden, which are generally sold by MSG Entertainment to corporate
customers via multi-year licenses. Under standard licenses, the licensee pays an annual license fee, which varies depending on the location and type of the suite or club. The license fee includes, for each seat in the suite or club, tickets for
Rangers home games, Knicks home games presented by MSG Sports, and other events at The Garden that are presented by MSG Entertainment for which tickets are sold to the general public, subject to certain exceptions. In addition, suite holders
separately pay for food and beverage service in their suites at The Garden. Food and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-alcoholic</FONT> beverage service is included in the annual license fee paid by club members. </P>

<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-exclusive</FONT> and generally permit a sponsor to use the name, logos and other trademarks of the Rangers and, in the case of sponsorship arrangements shared with MSG Sports, MSG Sports&#8217; brands in
connection with their own advertising, as well as in the case of sponsorship arrangements shared with MSG Entertainment, MSG Entertainment&#8217;s venues and brands in connection with their own advertising and in promotions in The Garden or in the
community. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Food, Beverage and Merchandise Sales </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We earn revenue from the sale of food and beverages during Rangers games at The Garden. In addition to concession-style sales of food and
beverages, which represent the majority of food and beverage revenues, The Garden also provides <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">higher-end</FONT> dining at premium clubs as well as catering for suites. Pursuant to the Arena License Agreement, the
Rangers receive 50% of net profits from the sales of food and beverages during their games at The Garden. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We also earn revenues from the
sale of Rangers merchandise both through the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-venue</FONT> and online sale of items bearing the logos or other marks of the Rangers and through our share of NHL distributions of royalties and other revenues from
the NHL&#8217;s licensing of team and sports league trademarks, which are generally shared equally among the teams in the NHL. Pursuant to the Arena License Agreement, the Rangers pay MSG Entertainment a commission equal to 30% of revenues from the
sales of their merchandise at The Garden. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Other </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Amounts collected for ticket sales, media rights, suite licenses and clubs, sponsorships, and venue signage in advance of the Company&#8217;s
satisfaction of its contractual performance obligations are recorded as deferred revenue and are recognized as revenues when earned. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Expenses </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our most significant expenses are player and other team personnel salaries. We also incur costs for travel, player insurance, league operating
assessments, NHL revenue sharing, and charges for transactions relating to players for career-ending and season-ending injuries, trades, and waivers and contract termination costs of players and other team personnel, including coaches and team
executives. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Arena License Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the Arena License Agreement provides for fixed payments to be made from inception through June&nbsp;30, 2055 in 12 equal
installments during each year of the contractual term. The contracted license fee for the first full contract year ended June&nbsp;30, 2021 was approximately $16,700, and then for each subsequent year, the license fee is 103% of the license fee for
the immediately preceding contract year. Recognition of operating lease costs is recorded on a straight-line basis as Rangers pre/regular season home games are played based upon the value of total future payments under the arrangement. Operating
lease costs associated with the Rangers playing home games at The Garden included (i) $19,344, $18,781 and $18,234 of expense paid in cash for Fiscal Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and (ii)&nbsp;a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> expense of $9,489, $10,052 and $10,599 for Fiscal Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Player
Salaries, Escrow System/Revenue Sharing </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The amount we pay an individual player is typically determined by negotiation between the
player (typically represented by an agent) and us, and is generally influenced by the player&#8217;s past performance, the amounts paid to players with comparable past performance by other sports teams, and restrictions in the NHL CBA, including the
salary floor and cap. The NHL CBA contains restrictions on when players may move between league clubs following expiration of their contracts and what rights their current and former clubs have. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>NHL CBA</I>. The current NHL CBA was scheduled to expire on September&nbsp;15, 2026. On July&nbsp;8, 2025, the NHL and the National Hockey
League Players&#8217; Association announced that a new four-year CBA had been ratified by the NHL Board of Governors and the NHL players. The new NHL CBA will be effective on September&nbsp;15, 2026 and expires after the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2029-30</FONT> season. The NHL CBA provides for a salary floor (i.e., a floor on each team&#8217;s aggregate player salaries) and a &#8220;hard&#8221; salary cap (i.e., teams may not exceed a stated maximum), which are
adjusted each season based upon league-wide revenues. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>NHL Escrow System/Revenue Sharing</I>. The NHL CBA, applicable prior to the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2026-27</FONT> season, provides that each season the NHL players in the aggregate receive as player compensation 50% of that season&#8217;s league-wide revenues. Because the aggregate amount to be paid to the players is
based upon league-wide revenues and not on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">team-by-team</FONT></FONT> basis, the Company may pay its players a higher or lower percentage of the Rangers&#8217; revenues than other
NHL teams pay of their own revenues. In order to implement the escrow system, NHL teams may withhold a portion of each player&#8217;s salary and contribute the withheld amounts to an escrow account. If the league&#8217;s aggregate player
compensation for a season exceeds the designated percentage (50%) of that season&#8217;s league-wide revenues, the excess is retained by the league. Any such excess funds are distributed to all teams in equal shares. In addition, the NHL CBA limits
the amount of deductions to be withheld from player salaries each year. If annual escrow deductions from player salaries are insufficient to limit league-wide player salaries to 50% of that season&#8217;s league-wide revenues, any shortfall will be
carried forward to future seasons and remain due from the players to the league. If the league&#8217;s aggregate player compensation for a season is less than the designated percentage (50%) of that season&#8217;s league-wide revenues, the
deficiency is collected from the teams and distributed to the players. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The NHL CBA also provides for a revenue sharing plan. The plan
generally requires the distribution of a pool of funds not more than 6.055% of league-wide revenues to certain qualifying lower-revenue teams and is funded as follows: (a) 50% from contributions by the top ten revenue earning teams (based on
preseason and </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">72 </P>

</DIV></Center>

regular season revenues, net of arena costs) in accordance with a formula; (b)&nbsp;then from payments by teams participating in the playoffs, with each team contributing 35% of its gate receipts
for each home playoff game; and (c)&nbsp;the remainder from centrally-generated NHL sources. Our net provisions for revenue sharing, net of escrow, for Fiscal Years 2026 and 2025 were approximately $43,530 and $43,828, respectively. The actual
amounts for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2025-26</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2024-25</FONT> seasons may vary significantly from the recorded provision based on actual operating results for the league and all NHL teams for the
season and other factors. The Rangers are consistently among the top ten revenue earning teams and, accordingly, have consistently contributed to the top ten revenue earning teams component of the plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The new NHL CBA, which is applicable starting with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2026-27</FONT> season, includes certain changes to
league rules and regulations, including replacing one preseason home game with a regular season home game, and changes to the revenue sharing plan which, beginning with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2026-27</FONT> season, will be funded as
follows: (a) 50% from contributions by the top eleven revenue earning teams (based on preseason and regular season revenues, net of arena costs) in accordance with a formula; (b)&nbsp;then from payments by teams participating in the playoffs, with
each team contributing 35% of its gate receipts for each home playoff game in the first round of the playoffs and 50% of its gate receipts for each home playoff game in subsequent playoff rounds; and (c)&nbsp;the remainder from centrally-generated
NHL sources. The Rangers are consistently among the top eleven revenue earning teams and, accordingly, are expected to contribute to the top eleven revenue earning teams component of the plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Other Team Operating Expenses </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a
member of the NHL, the Rangers are also subject to league assessments, which include certain operating costs incurred by the NHL to operate the league. The governing body of the NHL determines the amount of each season&#8217;s league assessments
that are required from each member team. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Direct variable
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-of-event</FONT></FONT> costs incurred at The Garden, such as the costs of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">front-of-house</FONT></FONT> and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">back-of-house</FONT></FONT> staff, including electricians, laborers, box office staff, ushers, security, and event production, are charged to the Company, and we also incur costs associated
with VIP amenities provided to certain ticket holders. The Rangers also pay expenses associated with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> operations, including for travel and player insurance.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, our team operating expenses include operating costs of the Company&#8217;s training center in Greenburgh, NY. The operation
of the Hartford Wolf Pack is reported as a net Rangers player development expense. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Other Expenses </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other expenses primarily include selling, general and administrative expenses that consist of (i)&nbsp;administrative costs, including
compensation, and professional fees, (ii)&nbsp;fees related to the Company&#8217;s sponsorship sales and service representation agreement, entered into in April 2020 (the &#8220;Sponsorship Sales and Service Representation Agreement&#8221;), and
(iii)&nbsp;sales and marketing costs. In addition, selling, general and administrative expenses includes allocations from MSG Sports for certain support functions that are provided on a centralized basis and not historically recorded at the
component level by MSG Sports, such as expenses related to executive management, finance, legal, human resources, government affairs, information technology and corporate operating lease costs. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Factors Affecting Operating Results </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>General </U></I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our
operating results are largely dependent on the continued popularity and/or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT> competitiveness of the Rangers, which have a direct effect on ticket sales for the team&#8217;s home games and are the
team&#8217;s largest single </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">73 </P>

</DIV></Center>

source of revenue. In addition, the popularity of the Rangers can generate fan enthusiasm, resulting in sustained premium seating, suite, sponsorship, food and beverage and merchandise sales.
Furthermore, success in the regular season may qualify the Rangers for participation in post-season playoffs, which provides us with a significant source of additional revenue, operating income and adjusted operating income. As with other sports
teams, the competitive position of the Rangers depends primarily on our ability to develop, obtain and retain talented players, for which we compete with other professional hockey teams. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A significant factor in our ability to attract and retain talented players is player compensation. The Company&#8217;s operating results
reflect the impact of high costs for player salaries and salaries of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-player</FONT> team personnel<I>.</I> In addition, we have incurred significant charges for costs associated with transactions relating to our
players for season-ending and career-ending injuries and for trades, waivers and contract terminations of players and other team personnel, including team executives<I>. </I>Waiver and termination costs reflect our efforts to improve the
competitiveness of the Rangers<I>.</I> These transactions can result in significant charges as the Company recognizes the estimated ultimate costs of these events in the period in which they occur, although amounts due to these individuals are
generally paid over their remaining contract terms<I>.</I> For example, the expenses for these transactions were a net provision of $4,628, $13,201 and $2,281 for Fiscal Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively<I>.</I> These expenses add to the
volatility of our operating results<I>.</I> We expect to continue to pursue opportunities to improve the overall quality of the Rangers and our efforts may result in continued significant expenses and charges<I>.</I> Such expenses and charges may
result in future operating losses although it is not possible to predict their timing or amount. In addition, our performance has been, and may in the future be, impacted by work stoppages. See &#8220;&#8212; Risk Factors &#8212; Economic and
Business Relationship Risks &#8212;<I>Labor matters may have a material negative effect on our business and results of operations</I>.&#8221; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to our future performance being dependent upon the continued popularity and/or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">on-ice</FONT>
competitiveness of the Rangers, it is also dependent on general economic conditions, in particular those in the New York City metropolitan area, and the effect of these conditions on our customers. An economic downturn could adversely affect our
business and results of operations as it may lead to lower demand for suite licenses and tickets to the games of the Rangers, which would also negatively affect merchandise and concession sales, as well as decrease levels of sponsorship and venue
signage revenues. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Amendment to Local Telecast Rights Agreement </U></I></P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Selling, general and administrative expenses </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily consist of (i)&nbsp;administrative costs, including compensation, and professional fees, (ii)&nbsp;fees
related to the Company&#8217;s Sponsorship Sales and Service Representation Agreement, and (iii)&nbsp;sales and marketing costs. In addition, selling, general and administrative expenses includes allocations from MSG Sports for certain support
functions that are provided on a centralized basis and not historically recorded at the component level by MSG Sports, such as expenses related to executive management, finance, legal, human resources, government affairs, information technology and
corporate operating lease costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses generally do not fluctuate in line with changes in the Company&#8217;s revenues and direct operating expenses. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Selling, general and administrative expenses for Fiscal Year 2026 increased $5,215, or 5%, to $101,557 as compared to Fiscal Year 2025 primarily due to
(i)&nbsp;higher corporate allocations from MSG Sports related to employee compensation and related benefits of $4,140, including executive management transition costs of $2,626 recognized in Fiscal Year 2026, (ii) corporate allocations from MSG
Sports related to the Distribution of $1,370, (iii)&nbsp;higher corporate allocations from MSG Sports related to MSG&nbsp;Sports&#8217; services agreement with MSG&nbsp;Entertainment of $1,122 and (iv)&nbsp;higher other general and administrative
expenses. This increase was partially offset by lower professional fees of $2,182. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Restructuring charges </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Restructuring charges for Fiscal Year 2026 were $1,234 due to termination benefits provided as part of a voluntary exit program the Company implemented during
Fiscal Year 2026. There were no restructuring charges for Fiscal Year 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Operating loss </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Operating loss for Fiscal Year 2026 increased $7,215, or 31%, to $30,474 as compared to Fiscal Year 2025 primarily due to higher direct operating expenses and
higher selling, general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher revenues. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Income taxes </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Income tax benefit for Fiscal Year 2026 of $7,772 reflects an effective tax rate of 23%. The effective tax rate differs from the income tax benefit derived
from applying the statutory federal rate of 21% to pretax loss primarily due to state and local tax benefit of $2,659, partially offset by income tax expense from nondeductible officers&#8217; compensation of $1,427 and nondeductible disability
insurance premiums of $534. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Income tax benefit for Fiscal Year 2025 of $4,810 reflects an effective tax rate of 17%. The effective tax rate differs from
the income tax benefit derived from applying the statutory federal rate of 21% to pretax loss </P>

(loss)</I> </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company evaluates performance based on several factors, of which the key financial measure is operating income (loss) excluding
(i)&nbsp;depreciation, amortization and impairments of property and equipment, goodwill and other intangible assets, (ii)&nbsp;share-based compensation expense or benefit, (iii)&nbsp;restructuring charges or credits, (iv)&nbsp;gains or losses on
sales or dispositions of businesses, and (v)&nbsp;the impact of purchase accounting adjustments related to business acquisitions, which is referred to as adjusted operating income (loss), a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measure.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Management believes that the exclusion of share-based compensation expense allows investors to better track the performance of the Company&#8217;s
business without regard to the settlement of an obligation that is not expected to be made in cash. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company believes adjusted operating income (loss)
is an appropriate measure for evaluating the operating performance of the Company. Adjusted operating income (loss) and similar measures with similar titles are common performance measures used by investors and analysts to analyze the
Company&#8217;s performance. The Company uses revenues and adjusted operating income (loss) measures as the most important indicators of its business performance and evaluates management&#8217;s effectiveness with specific reference to these
indicators. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Adjusted operating income (loss) should be viewed as a supplement to and not a substitute for operating income (loss), net income (loss),
cash flows from operating activities, and other measures of performance and/or liquidity presented in accordance with GAAP. Since adjusted operating income (loss) is not a measure of performance calculated in accordance with GAAP, this measure may
not be comparable to similar measures with similar titles used by other companies. The Company has presented the components that reconcile operating income (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, to adjusted operating income
(loss). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following is a reconciliation of operating loss to adjusted operating loss: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Selling, general and administrative expenses </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Selling, general and administrative expenses for Fiscal Year 2025 decreased $7,799, or 7%, to $96,342 as compared to Fiscal Year 2024 primarily due to
(i)&nbsp;lower corporate allocations from MSG Sports related to employee compensation and related benefits of $7,505, primarily related to executive management transition costs of $4,094 recognized in Fiscal Year 2024, (ii) lower playoff related
expenses of $4,812 and (iii)&nbsp;lower sales and marketing costs of $1,879, partially offset by (iv)&nbsp;higher corporate allocations from MSG Sports related to MSG Sports operating leases of $2,780 and (v)&nbsp;higher professional fees of $2,202.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Operating (loss) income </U></I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Operating (loss)
income for Fiscal Year 2025 reflected an operating loss of $23,259 and operating (loss) income for Fiscal Year 2024 reflected operating income of $26,833. The decrease was primarily due to lower revenues, partially offset by lower direct operating
expenses and lower selling, general and administrative expenses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Interest expense </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest expense for Fiscal Year 2025 decreased $4,203, or 51%, to $4,065 as compared to Fiscal Year 2024, primarily due to lower average borrowings under the
Rangers Revolving Credit Facility in Fiscal Year 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Income taxes </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Income tax benefit for Fiscal Year 2025 of $4,810 reflects an effective tax rate of 17%. The effective tax rate differs from the income tax benefit derived
from applying the statutory federal rate of 21% to pretax loss primarily due to income tax expense from nondeductible officers&#8217; compensation of $1,931 and nondeductible disability insurance premiums of $595, partially offset by state and local
tax benefit of $1,783. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Income tax expense for Fiscal Year 2024 of $11,024 reflects an effective tax rate of 60%. The effective tax rate differs from the
income tax expense derived from applying the statutory federal rate of 21% to pretax income primarily due to income tax expense from state and local taxes of $4,206, nondeductible officers&#8217; compensation of $2,153 and nondeductible disability
insurance premiums of $547. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See Note 16 to the Audited Combined Annual Financial Statements included elsewhere in this information statement for further
details on the components of income tax and a reconciliation of the statutory federal rate to the effective tax rate. Income taxes recognized in the combined financial statements and resulting effective tax rates may not be reflective of the taxes
that the Company expects to recognize in the future as a standalone entity. </P>
