operating (loss) income for Fiscal Year 2024 reflected adjusted operating income of $37,128. The decrease was primarily due to lower revenues, partially offset by lower direct operating expenses and lower selling, general and administrative
expenses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Liquidity and Capital Resources </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Overview </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our primary sources of liquidity are cash
and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations, transfers from MSG Sports and MSG Sports&#8217; subsidiaries, and available borrowing capacity under the 2025 Rangers Revolving Credit Facility. See Note 12 to the Audited Combined Annual Financial
Statements included elsewhere in this information statement for a discussion of the 2025 Rangers Revolving Credit Facility and the Rangers NHL Advance Agreement (each as defined therein). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our principal uses of cash include the operation of our businesses, working capital-related items, transfers to MSG Sports and MSG Sports&#8217; subsidiaries,
and the repayment of outstanding debt, including under the Rangers NHL Advance Agreement. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports uses a centralized approach to cash management and
financing of operations. Cash is managed centrally with net earnings reinvested and working capital requirements met from existing liquid funds. The Company&#8217;s cash has been regularly &#8220;swept&#8221; historically. Cash and cash equivalents
were attributed to the Company for each of the periods presented, as such cash was held in accounts legally owned by the Company. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of June&nbsp;30,
2026, the Company had $160 in Cash and cash equivalents. In addition, as of&nbsp;June&nbsp;30, 2026, the Company&#8217;s deferred revenue obligations were $56,951, net of billed, but not yet collected deferred revenue.&nbsp;This balance is primarily
comprised of obligations in connection with tickets and suites. The outstanding balance under the Rangers NHL Advance Agreement was $16,500 as of June&nbsp;30, 2026. There were no borrowings under the 2025 Rangers Revolving Credit Facility as of
June&nbsp;30, 2026. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We regularly monitor and assess our ability to meet our net funding and investing requirements. The decisions of the Company as to
the use of its available liquidity will be based upon the ongoing review of the funding needs of the business, management&#8217;s view of a favorable allocation of cash resources, and the timing of cash flow generation. To the extent the Company
desires to access alternative sources of funding through the capital and credit markets, restrictions imposed by the NHL and potentially challenging U.S. and global economic and market conditions could adversely impact its ability to do so at that
time. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We believe we have sufficient liquidity, including $160 in Cash and cash equivalents as of June&nbsp;30, 2026, along with $250,000 of additional
available borrowing capacity under the 2025 Rangers Revolving Credit Facility (as of June&nbsp;30, 2026), to fund our operations and satisfy any obligations, for the foreseeable future. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Operating Activities </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in operating activities for Fiscal Year 2026 increased $45,420 to $48,661 as compared to Fiscal Year 2025. The change was primarily due to the
impact of changes in working capital assets and liabilities, partially offset by the change in net loss adjusted for non-cash items. The changes in working capital assets and liabilities were primarily driven by (i) an increase in net related party
receivables of $22,773 primarily due to the timing of collections related to the Company&#8217;s Arena License Agreement and Sponsorship Sales and Service Representation Agreement, (ii) a decrease in accrued and other liabilities of $21,805
primarily due to higher payments related to league revenue sharing, net of escrow in Fiscal Year 2026, partially offset by the timing of payments related to employee compensation, and (iii) a decrease in deferred revenue of $15,179 primarily due to
the timing of collections of ticket and suites sales in advance of recognition. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in operating activities for Fiscal Year 2025 was $3,241 as
compared to net cash provided by operating activities for Fiscal Year 2024 of $6,096. The change was primarily due to the change in net (loss) income adjusted for non-cash items, offset by the impact of changes in working capital assets and
liabilities. The changes in working capital assets and liabilities were primarily driven by (i) a decrease in net related party receivables of $20,326, primarily due to the timing of collections related to the Company&#8217;s Arena License Agreement
and Sponsorship Sales and Service Representation Agreement, (ii) an increase in deferred revenue of $17,667, primarily due to higher collections of ticket sales in advance of recognition and (iii) an increase in accrued and other liabilities of
$7,829, primarily due to increased accruals for league revenue sharing and league assessments in Fiscal Year 2025. These changes were partially offset by an increase in prepaid expenses and other assets of $6,405 primarily driven by the timing of
payments related to employee compensation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Investing Activities </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in investing activities for Fiscal Year 2026 increased by $162 to $634 as compared to Fiscal Year 2025 due to higher capital expenditures in
Fiscal Year 2026. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in investing activities for Fiscal Year 2025 decreased by $174 to $472 as compared to Fiscal Year 2024 due to lower
capital expenditures in Fiscal Year 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I><U>Financing Activities </U></I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash provided by financing activities for Fiscal Year 2026 increased by $34,075 to $40,735 as compared to Fiscal Year 2025. The increase was primarily due
to higher net transfers from MSG Sports and MSG Sports&#8217; subsidiaries in Fiscal Year 2026, partially offset by payments for financing costs in Fiscal Year 2026 and higher principal repayments under the Rangers NHL Advance Agreement in Fiscal
Year 2026. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash provided by financing activities for Fiscal Year 2025 increased $6,404 to $6,660 as compared to Fiscal Year 2024. The increase was
primarily due to principal repayments under the Rangers Revolving Credit Facility in Fiscal Year 2024, partially offset by lower net transfers from MSG Sports and MSG Sports&#8217; subsidiaries in Fiscal Year 2025, additional borrowings under the
Rangers Revolving Credit Facility in Fiscal Year 2024 and, to a lesser extent, the impact of principal repayments under the Rangers NHL Advance Agreement in Fiscal Year 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Seasonality of Our Business </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s
dependence on revenues from the Rangers generally means that it earns a disproportionate share of its revenues in the second and third quarters of the Company&#8217;s fiscal year, which is when the majority of the team&#8217;s games are played. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><U>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements and Critical Accounting Estimates </U></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See Note
2 the Audited Combined Annual Financial Statements included elsewhere in this information statement for discussion of recently issued accounting pronouncements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Critical Accounting Estimates </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of
the combined financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions about future events. These estimates and the underlying assumptions affect the amounts of assets and liabilities reported, disclosures
about contingent assets and liabilities, and reported amounts of revenues and expenses. Management believes its use of estimates in the combined financial statements to be reasonable. In addition to the critical accounting estimates disclosed below,
refer to the section above entitled <I>Proposed Distribution and Basis of Presentation</I> for further details on corporate allocations recorded in the combined financial statements. The significant accounting policies which we believe are the most
critical to aid in fully understanding and evaluating our reported financial results include the following: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Arrangements with Multiple Performance
Obligations </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has contracts with customers, including multi-year sponsorship agreements, that contain multiple performance obligations.
Payment terms for such arrangements can vary by contract, but payments are generally due in installments throughout the contractual term. The performance obligations included in each sponsorship agreement vary and may include various advertising
benefits such as, but not limited to, signage, digital advertising, and event or property specific advertising, as well as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-advertising</FONT> benefits such as suite licenses and event tickets. To the extent the
Company&#8217;s multi-year arrangements provide for performance obligations that are consistent over the multi-year contractual term, such performance obligations generally meet the definition of a series as provided for under the accounting
guidance. If performance obligations meet the definition of a series, the contractual fees for all years during the contract term are aggregated and the related revenue is recognized proportionately as the underlying performance obligations are
satisfied. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The timing of revenue recognition for each performance obligation is dependent upon the facts and circumstances surrounding the
Company&#8217;s satisfaction of its respective performance obligation. The Company allocates the transaction price for such arrangements to each performance obligation within the arrangement based on the estimated relative standalone selling price
of the performance obligation. The Company&#8217;s process for determining its estimated standalone selling prices involves management&#8217;s judgment and considers multiple factors including company specific and market specific factors that may
vary depending upon the unique facts and circumstances related to each performance obligation. Key factors considered by the Company in developing an estimated standalone selling price for its performance obligations include, but are not limited to,
prices charged for similar performance obligations, the Company&#8217;s ongoing pricing strategy and policies, and consideration of pricing of similar performance obligations sold in other arrangements with multiple performance obligations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company may incur costs to obtain its multi-year sponsorship agreements. The Company assesses such costs for capitalization on a contract by contract
basis. To the extent costs are capitalized, the Company estimates the useful life of the related contract asset which may be the underlying contract term or the estimated customer life depending on the facts and circumstances surrounding the
contract. The contract asset is amortized over the estimated useful life. </P>

and assumptions regarding future cash flows and other factors to determine the fair value of the respective assets. These estimates and assumptions could have a significant impact on whether an impairment charge is recognized and also the magnitude
of any such charge. Fair value estimates are made at a specific point in time, based on relevant information. These estimates are subjective in nature and involve significant uncertainties and judgments and therefore cannot be determined with
precision. Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates. If these estimates or material related assumptions change in the future, the Company may be required to record impairment charges related to its long-lived and/or
indefinite-lived assets. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Goodwill </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Goodwill is
tested annually for impairment as of August&nbsp;31<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">st</SUP> and at any time upon the occurrence of certain events or changes in circumstances. The Company performs its goodwill impairment test at the
reporting unit level, which is the same as or one level below the operating segment level. The Company has one operating and reportable segment, and as of June&nbsp;30, 2026, the Company had one reporting unit for goodwill impairment testing
purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has the option to perform a qualitative assessment to determine if an impairment is more likely than not to have occurred. If the
Company can support the conclusion that it is not more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, the Company would not need to perform a quantitative impairment test for that reporting unit. If the
Company cannot support such a conclusion or the Company does not elect to perform the qualitative assessment, a quantitative assessment is performed by comparing the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount, including goodwill. The
estimates of the fair value of the Company&#8217;s reporting units are primarily determined using discounted cash flows and comparable market transactions. These valuations are based on estimates and assumptions including projected future cash
flows, discount rates, determination of appropriate market comparables and the determination of whether a premium or discount should be applied to comparables. Significant judgments inherent in a discounted cash flow analysis include the selection
of the appropriate discount rate, the estimate of the amount and timing of projected future cash flows and identification of appropriate continuing growth rate assumptions. The discount rates used in the analysis are intended to reflect the risk
inherent in the projected future cash flows. The amount of an impairment loss is measured as the amount by which a reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value exceeds its fair value, not to exceed the carrying amount of goodwill. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For purposes of the combined financial statements, goodwill was recorded on the basis of the historical goodwill of MSG Sports components. Goodwill impairment

</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has the option to perform a qualitative assessment to determine if an impairment is more likely than not to have occurred. In the qualitative
assessment, the Company must evaluate the totality of qualitative factors, including any recent fair value measurements, that impact whether an indefinite-lived intangible asset other than goodwill has a carrying amount that more likely than not
exceeds its fair value. The Company must proceed to conducting a quantitative analysis if the Company (i)&nbsp;determines that such an impairment is more likely than not to exist, or (ii)&nbsp;forgoes the qualitative assessment entirely. Under the
quantitative assessment, the impairment test for identifiable indefinite-lived intangible assets consists of a comparison of the estimated fair value of the intangible asset with its carrying value. If the carrying value of the intangible asset
exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess. For all periods presented, the Company elected to perform a qualitative assessment of impairment for the indefinite-lived intangible assets. These
assessments considered the events and circumstances that could affect the significant inputs used to determine the fair value of the intangible asset. Examples of such events and circumstances include: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Lease Accounting </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company is party to the Arena
License Agreement, which is a long term license agreement with MSG Entertainment that ends June&nbsp;30, 2055 that allows the Rangers to play their home games at The Garden. The Company accounts for the rights of use of The Garden pursuant to the
Arena License Agreement as a lease under the ASC Topic 842, Leases. The Company determines whether an arrangement contains a lease at the inception </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">87 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
of the arrangement. If a lease is determined to exist, the lease term is assessed based on the date when the underlying asset is made available for the Company&#8217;s use by the lessor. The
Company&#8217;s assessment of the lease term reflects the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cancelable</FONT> term of the lease, inclusive of any rent-free periods and/or periods covered by early-termination options which the Company is
reasonably certain not to exercise, as well as periods covered by renewal options which the Company is reasonably certain of exercising. The Company also determines lease classification as either operating or finance at lease commencement, which
governs the pattern of expense recognition and the presentation reflected in the combined statements of operations and comprehensive (loss) income over the lease term. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For leases with a term exceeding 12 months, a lease liability is recorded in the combined balance sheet at lease commencement reflecting the present value of
the fixed minimum payment obligations over the lease term. A corresponding <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">right-of-use</FONT></FONT> (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) asset equal to the initial lease liability is also recorded,
adjusted for any prepaid rent and/or initial direct costs incurred in connection with execution of the lease and reduced by any lease incentives received. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company includes fixed payment obligations related to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-lease</FONT> components in the measurement of ROU assets and
lease liabilities, as the Company has elected to account for lease and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-lease</FONT> components together as a single lease component. ROU assets associated with finance leases, if any, are presented separate from
operating leases ROU assets and are included within Property and equipment, net in the combined balance sheets. For purposes of measuring the present value of the Company&#8217;s fixed payment obligations for a given lease, the Company uses its
incremental borrowing rate, determined based on information available at lease commencement, as rates implicit in the underlying leasing arrangements are typically not readily determinable. The Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate reflects the
rate it would pay to borrow on a secured basis and incorporates the term and economic environment surrounding the associated lease. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For operating leases,
fixed lease payments are recognized as lease expense on a straight-line basis over the lease term. For finance leases, the initial ROU asset is depreciated on a straight-line basis over the lease term, along with recognition of interest expense
associated with accretion of the lease liability, which is ultimately reduced by the related fixed payments. For leases with a term of 12 months or less (&#8220;short-term leases&#8221;), any fixed lease payments are recognized on a straight-line
basis over the lease term and are not recognized in the combined balance sheet. Variable lease costs for both operating and finance leases, if any, are recognized as incurred and such costs are excluded from lease balances recorded in the combined
balance sheet. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In certain instances, leases include options to renew, with varying option terms. The exercise of lease renewal, if available under the
lease options, is generally at the Company&#8217;s discretion and is considered in the Company&#8217;s assessment of the respective lease term. The Company&#8217;s lease agreements do not contain material residual value guarantees or material
restrictive covenants. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Arena License Agreement provides for fixed payments to be made from inception through June&nbsp;30, 2055 in 12 equal
installments during each year of the contractual term. The contracted license fee for the first full contract year ended June&nbsp;30, 2021 was approximately $16,700, and then for each subsequent year, the license fee is 103% of the license fee for
the immediately preceding contract year. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Rangers are entitled to use The Garden on home game days, which are usually nonconsecutive, for a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-defined</FONT> period of time before and after the game. In evaluating the Company&#8217;s lease cost, the Company considered the timing of payments throughout the lease term and the nonconsecutive periods of use,
provided for within the license. While payments are made throughout the contract year in twelve equal installments under the arrangement, the periods of use only span each of the Rangers pre/regular season home games. As such, the Company concluded
that the related straight-line operating lease costs should be recorded equally as Rangers pre/regular season home games are played. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As part of the Arena
License Agreement, we recognized license fees which are characterized as operating lease liabilities and ROU assets. We measured the lease liabilities at the present value of the future lease payments as
</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc127770_11"></A>CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Corporate Governance </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>General </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will apply to list our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock on the NYSE&nbsp;under the symbol &#8220;MSGR&#8221; (and change our name to &#8220;MSG
Rangers Corp.&#8221;) and Madison Square Garden Sports Corp. will change its symbol on the NYSE to &#8220;MSGK&#8221; (and be renamed &#8220;MSG Knickerbockers Corp.&#8221;) in connection with the Distribution. As a result, we will be generally
subject to NYSE corporate governance listing standards. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A listed company that meets NYSE&#8217;s definition of a &#8220;controlled
company&#8221; may elect not to comply with certain of these requirements. We have been informed that prior to the Distribution, the members of the Dolan Family Group will enter into a Stockholders Agreement with respect to the voting of their
shares of the Class&nbsp;B Common Stock that will be issued in the Distribution. As a result, following the Distribution, we will be a &#8220;controlled company.&#8221; As a controlled company, we will have the right to elect not to comply with the
corporate governance rules of the NYSE requiring: (i)&nbsp;a majority of independent directors on our Board, (ii)&nbsp;an independent corporate governance and nominating committee and (iii)&nbsp;an independent compensation committee. Our Board of
Directors has elected for the Company to be treated as a &#8220;controlled company&#8221; under NYSE corporate governance rules and not to comply with the NYSE requirement for a majority-independent board of directors and for a corporate governance
and nominating committee because of our status as a controlled company. Nevertheless, we expect our Board of Directors to elect to comply with the NYSE requirement for an independent compensation committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the consideration of the Distribution by MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors, a committee of MSG Sports&#8217; board of
directors, comprising three independent Class&nbsp;A Directors, recommended to the full MSG Sports board of directors the principal elements of our governance structure, including the replication in our amended and restated articles of incorporation
of the MSG Sports common stock voting structure, which the MSG Sports board adopted as part of its approval of the filing with the SEC of the registration statement, of which this information statement forms a part. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Corporate Governance Guidelines </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our
Board of Directors will adopt our Corporate Governance Guidelines (&#8220;Governance Guidelines&#8221;). These guidelines set forth our practices and policies with respect to Board composition and selection, Board meetings, executive sessions of the
Board, Board committees, the expectations we have of our directors, selection of the Executive Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer, management succession, Board and executive compensation, and Board self-assessment requirements. The full text
of our Governance Guidelines will be available at our website at investor.msgrangers.com under Investors &#8212; Governance &#8212; Corporate Governance. A copy may be obtained by writing to MSGS Spinco, Inc., Two Pennsylvania Plaza, New York,
NY&nbsp;10121; Attention: Corporate Secretary. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Executive Sessions of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Management</FONT> and Independent Board
Members </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under our Governance Guidelines, either our directors who are not also executive officers of our Company (the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;non-management</FONT> directors&#8221;) or our directors who are independent under the NYSE rules are required to meet regularly in executive sessions with no members of management present. If <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> directors who are not independent participate in these executive sessions, the independent directors under the NYSE rules are required to meet separately in executive sessions at least once each year.
The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> or independent directors may specify the procedure to designate the director who may preside at any such executive session. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Communicating with Our Directors </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our
Board will adopt policies designed to allow our stockholders and other interested parties to communicate with our directors. Any interested party who wishes to communicate directly with the Board or any
</P>

information concerning our Director Stock Plan. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-employee</FONT> directors have the ability to make a

stock units in lieu of cash compensation are determined by dividing the value of the applicable director&#8217;s total annual cash compensation by the average closing price over the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">twenty-trading-day</FONT> period
concluding on the date immediately preceding the grant date (February 15 or the next succeeding business day). Restricted stock units are fully vested on the date of grant but remain subject to a holding requirement until the first business day
following 90 days after a separation from service (other than in the event of a director&#8217;s death, in which case they are settled as soon as practicable), at which time they are settled in stock or, at the election of the compensation committee
of the Board (the &#8220;Compensation Committee&#8221;), in cash. Such equity grants are made pursuant to the Company&#8217;s 2026 Stock Plan for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Directors (the &#8220;Director Stock Plan&#8221;).
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Board Committees </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board has two
permanent committees: the Audit Committee and the Compensation Committee. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Audit Committee </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the time of the Distribution, our Audit Committee will consist of three members. The primary purposes and responsibilities of our Audit
Committee are to: (a)&nbsp;assist the Board (i)&nbsp;in its oversight of the integrity of our financial statements, (ii)&nbsp;in its oversight of our compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, (iii)&nbsp;in assessing our independent
registered public accounting firm&#8217;s qualifications and independence, and (iv)&nbsp;in assessing the performance of our internal audit function and independent registered public accounting firm; (b)&nbsp;appoint, compensate, retain, oversee and
terminate the Company&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approve,</FONT> or adopt appropriate procedures to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approve,</FONT> all audit and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services, if any, to be provided by the independent registered public accounting firm; (c)&nbsp;review the appointment and replacement of the head of our internal audit department and to review and
coordinate the agenda, scope, priorities, plan and authority of the internal audit department; (d)&nbsp;establish procedures for the receipt, retention and treatment of complaints received by the Company regarding accounting, internal accounting
controls or auditing matters and for the confidential, anonymous submission by Company employees or any provider of accounting-related services of concerns regarding questionable accounting and auditing matters and review of submissions and the
treatment of any such complaints; (e)&nbsp;review and approve related party transactions that are required to be disclosed under SEC rules or that require such approval under the Company&#8217;s Related Party Transaction Approval Policy (if the
Audit Committee is then serving as the Independent Committee under such policy); (f)&nbsp;conduct and review with the Board an annual self-assessment of the Audit Committee; (g)&nbsp;prepare any report of the Audit Committee required by the rules
and regulations of the SEC for inclusion in our annual proxy statement; (h)&nbsp;review and reassess the Audit Committee charter at least annually; (i)&nbsp;report to the Board on a regular basis; and (j)&nbsp;oversee corporate risks, including
cybersecurity and venue security, and provide periodic updates to the Board on such oversight activities. The text of our Audit Committee charter will be available on our website at investor.msgrangers.com under Investors &#8212; Governance &#8212;
Corporate Governance. A copy may be obtained by writing to MSGS Spinco, Inc., Two Pennsylvania Plaza, New York, NY 10121; Attention: Corporate Secretary. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expect our Board of Directors to determine that each member of our Audit Committee is
&#8220;independent&#8221; within the meaning of the rules of both the NYSE and the SEC, and that each has not participated in the preparation of the financial statements of the Company or any current subsidiary of the Company at any time during the
past three years and is able to read and understand fundamental financial statements, including balance sheets, income statements and cash flow statements. All directors we add to the Audit Committee in the future will also meet those standards. We
expect our Board to also determine that at least one member of our Audit Committee is an &#8220;audit committee financial expert&#8221; within the meaning of the rules of the SEC. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our Board has established a procedure whereby complaints or concerns with respect to accounting, internal controls, auditing and other matters
may be submitted to the Audit Committee. This procedure is described under &#8220;Communicating with Our Directors&#8221; above. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our
Audit Committee did not exist in Fiscal Year 2026. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Compensation Committee </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the time of the Distribution, our Compensation Committee will consist of three members. The primary purposes of our Compensation Committee
are to: (a)&nbsp;establish our general compensation philosophy and, in consultation with management, oversee the development and implementation of compensation programs; (b)&nbsp;review and approve corporate goals and objectives relevant to the
compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and our other executive officers who are required to file reports with the SEC under Section&nbsp;16 of the Exchange Act (together with the Chief Executive Officer, the &#8220;Senior Employees&#8221;),
evaluate their performance in light of these goals and objectives and determine and approve their compensation based upon that evaluation; (c)&nbsp;approve any new equity compensation plan or material changes to an existing plan; (d)&nbsp;oversee
the activities of the committee or committees administering our retirement and benefit plans; (e)&nbsp;in consultation with management, oversee regulatory compliance with respect to compensation matters including overseeing the Company&#8217;s
policies on structuring compensation programs to preserve tax deductibility; (f)&nbsp;determine and approve any severance or similar termination payments to be made to Senior Employees (current or former); (g)&nbsp;determine the components and
amount of Board compensation and review such determinations from time to time in relation to other similarly situated companies; (h)&nbsp;prepare any reports of the Compensation Committee to be included in the Company&#8217;s annual proxy statement
in accordance with the applicable rules and regulations of the SEC; (i)&nbsp;conduct and review with the Board an annual self-assessment of the Compensation Committee; and (j)&nbsp;report to the Board on a regular basis, but not less than annually.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Compensation Committee will review the performance of the Senior Employees, evaluate their performance in light of those goals and
objectives and, either as a committee or together with any other independent directors (as directed by the Board), will determine and approve the Senior Employees&#8217; compensation level based on this evaluation. In determining the long-term
incentive component of our Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s compensation, the Compensation Committee will consider, among other factors, the Company&#8217;s performance and relative stockholder return, the value of similar incentive awards to Chief
Executive Officers at comparable companies and the awards given to the Chief Executive Officer in past years. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Compensation Committee
may, in its discretion, delegate a portion of its duties and responsibilities to one or more subcommittees of the Compensation Committee. For example, the Compensation Committee may delegate the approval of certain transactions to a subcommittee
consisting solely of members of the Compensation Committee who are <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;non-employee</FONT> directors&#8221; for the purposes of Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">16b-3</FONT> issued by the SEC under the
Exchange Act. The Compensation Committee may also engage outside compensation consultants to assist in the performance of its duties and responsibilities. The text of our Compensation Committee charter will be available on our website at
investor.msgrangers.com under Investors &#8212; Governance &#8212; Corporate Governance. A copy may be obtained by writing to MSGS Spinco, Inc., Two Pennsylvania Plaza, New York, NY&nbsp;10121; Attention: Corporate Secretary. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Absence of Nominating Committee </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will
not have a nominating committee. We believe that it is appropriate not to have a nominating committee because of our stockholder voting structure. Under the terms of our amended and restated articles of incorporation, the holders of our Class&nbsp;B
Common Stock will have the right to elect up to 75% of the members of our Board. Our Governance Guidelines provide a mechanism for the selection of nominees for election as directors by the holders of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock
(&#8220;Class&nbsp;A Directors&#8221;) and by the holders of our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock (&#8220;Class&nbsp;B Directors&#8221;). The holders of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock will be entitled to elect at least 25% of the members of our Board. Under
our Governance Guidelines, nominees for election as Class&nbsp;A Directors shall be recommended to the Board by the Class&nbsp;A Directors then in office who were elected by the holders of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock. Nominees for election as
Class&nbsp;B Directors shall be recommended to our Board by the Class&nbsp;B Directors then in office who were elected by the holders of the Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our directors have not set specific, minimum qualifications that nominees must meet in order for them to be nominated for election to the
Board, but rather believe that each nominee should be evaluated based on his or her individual merits, taking into account, among other matters, the factors set forth in our Governance Guidelines under &#8220;Board Composition&#8221; and
&#8220;Selection of Directors.&#8221; Those factors include: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Other Committees </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to standing committees, the Company has adopted a policy whereby a committee of our Board of Directors consisting entirely of
independent directors (an &#8220;Independent Committee&#8221;) will review and approve transactions with Other Entities in which the value or expected value of the transaction or arrangement exceeds $1,000,000. The Independent Committee will also
review and approve or take such other action as it may deem appropriate with respect to transactions involving the Company and its subsidiaries, on the one hand, and in which any director, executive officer, greater than 5% stockholder of the
Company or any other &#8220;related person&#8221; as defined in Item&nbsp;404 of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Regulation&nbsp;S-K</FONT> adopted by the SEC (&#8220;Item&nbsp;404&#8221;) has or will have a direct or indirect material interest.
This approval requirement covers any transaction that meets the related party disclosure requirements of the SEC as set forth in Item&nbsp;404, which currently apply to any transaction (or any series of similar transactions) in which the amount
involved exceeds $120,000. The policy does not cover decisions on compensation or benefits or the hiring or retention of executive officers. The hiring or retention of executive officers is determined by our full Board of Directors. Compensation of
executive officers is subject to the approval of our Compensation Committee. This policy also does not cover any pro rata distributions to all Company stockholders, including a pro rata distribution of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock to holders of our
Class&nbsp;A Common Stock and our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock to holders of our Class&nbsp;B Common Stock. No director on an Independent Committee will participate in the consideration of a related party transaction with that director or any related
person of that director. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our amended and restated bylaws will provide for the formation of an Executive Committee of the Board of
Directors which would have the power to exercise all of the powers and authority of the Board in the management of the business and affairs of the Company, except as limited by the Nevada law. Our Board has not formed an Executive Committee,
although it could do so in the future. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our amended and restated bylaws will also permit the Board of Directors to appoint other

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc127770_12"></A>EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Introduction </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This section presents
information concerning compensation arrangements for our named executive officers. We present historical and current fiscal year information concerning the compensation from MSG Sports of Mr.&nbsp;James&nbsp;L. Dolan, our Executive Chairman and
Chief Executive Officer; Jamaal T. Lesane, our Executive Vice President and Chief Legal Officer (who served as the Chief Operating Officer of MSG Sports for Fiscal Year 2026); David Granville-Smith, our Executive Vice President; and Paul DiCicco,
our Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer for Fiscal Year 2026. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>The historical compensation information,
including in particular the information set forth below under &#8220;&#8212; Historical Compensation Information,&#8221; is not directly relevant to the compensation that these officers will receive from the Company. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Each of our named executive officers holds various long-term incentive awards that were granted by MSG Sports. Treatment of these in the
Distribution is described under &#8220;&#8212; Treatment of Outstanding Awards.&#8221; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Compensation Discussion&nbsp;&amp; Analysis </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This Compensation Discussion&nbsp;&amp; Analysis provides a discussion of MSG Sports&#8217; compensation philosophy and Fiscal Year 2026
compensation from MSG Sports for our NEOs (as defined below). MSG Sports&#8217; compensation philosophy may be relevant to the Company because it is anticipated that the elements of our compensation will be similar to the elements of MSG
Sports&#8217; compensation. Our Compensation Committee will review the impact of the Distribution and will review all aspects of compensation and make any appropriate adjustments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For purposes of this Compensation Discussion&nbsp;&amp; Analysis, the Company&#8217;s named executive officers are James L. Dolan, Jamaal T.
Lesane, David Granville-Smith and Paul DiCicco. These individuals are referred to as Named Executive Officers (&#8220;NEOs&#8221;). Messrs. Dolan, Lesane, Granville-Smith and DiCicco are also named executive officers of MSG Sports and will continue
as officers of MSG Sports following the Distribution. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Executive Summary </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>MSG Sports&#8217; Executive Compensation Program Objectives and Philosophy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports is a sports business comprised of dynamic and powerful assets and brands. It operates in specialized industries and its named
executive officers have substantial and meaningful professional experience in these industries. Given the unique nature of its business, MSG Sports places great importance on its ability to attract, retain, motivate and reward experienced named
executive officers who can continue to drive its business objectives and achieve strong financial, operational and stock price performance. The compensation committee of the board of directors of MSG Sports (&#8220;MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation
Committee&#8221; or the &#8220;MSG Sports Compensation Committee&#8221;) has designed executive compensation policies and programs that are consistent with, explicitly linked to, and supportive of the financial and strategic objectives of growing
MSG Sports&#8217; businesses and driving long-term stockholder value. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; program reflects four key overarching executive
compensation principles: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

Compensation Committee seeks to fulfill these objectives by maintaining appropriate balances between (1)&nbsp;short-term and long-term compensation, (2)&nbsp;cash and equity-based compensation, and (3)&nbsp;performance-based and time-based vesting
of compensation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Elements of MSG Sports&#8217; Fiscal Year 2026 Compensation&nbsp;&amp; Performance Objectives </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports compensates its named executive officers through base salary, annual incentive awards, long-term incentive awards, perquisites and
benefit programs. MSG Sports&#8217; annual and long-term incentive programs provide performance-based incentives for such named executive officers tied to key financial and strategic measures that generate long-term stockholder value and reward
sustained achievement of MSG Sports&#8217; key financial goals. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports considers revenues and AOI to be the key measures of its
operating performance. As such, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee has incorporated AOI and revenues in its long-term incentive performance awards (i.e., performance stock units) and AOI in its annual incentive awards. MSG Sports&#8217;
long-term incentive program also includes time-vested restricted stock units whose value is tied to the performance of the market value of MSG Sports Class&nbsp;A Common Stock. Mr.&nbsp;DiCicco, who joined MSG Sports effective May&nbsp;11, 2026, was
not eligible to receive annual incentive awards or long-term incentive awards during the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026. In order to further align compensation opportunities with MSG Sports&#8217; strategic vision and focus on growth, MSG
Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee has also occasionally granted certain awards in the form of stock options, where appropriate, which support the goal of generating long-term stockholder value. </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Program Practices and Policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following discussion describes the practices and policies implemented by MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee during the fiscal year
ended June&nbsp;30, 2026. Much of MSG Sports&#8217; named executive officers&#8217; compensation for the year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026 is covered by employment agreements approved by MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Role of the MSG Sports Compensation Committee </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee administers MSG Sports&#8217; executive compensation program. The responsibilities of MSG
Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee are set forth in its charter. Among other responsibilities, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee: (1)&nbsp;establishes MSG Sports&#8217; general compensation philosophy and, in consultation with management,
oversees the development and implementation of MSG Sports&#8217; compensation programs; (2)&nbsp;reviews and approves corporate goals and objectives relevant to the compensation of MSG Sports&#8217; executive officers who are required to file
reports with the SEC under Section&nbsp;16(a) of the Exchange Act, evaluates their performance in light of those goals and objectives, and determines and approves their respective compensation levels based on this evaluation; (3)&nbsp;oversees the
activities of the committee or committees administering MSG Sports&#8217; retirement and benefit plans; and (4)&nbsp;administers MSG Sports&#8217; stockholder-approved compensation plans. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In carrying out its responsibilities, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee utilizes the services of the MSG Sports independent
compensation consultant and independent legal counsel, and considers recommendations from management, each as further described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Role of the
MSG Sports Independent Compensation Consultant </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee has authority under its charter to engage
outside consultants to assist in the performance of its duties and responsibilities. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee utilizes the services of ClearBridge Compensation Group LLC (the &#8220;MSG Sports independent compensation
consultant&#8221;), an independent compensation consultant, to assist in determining whether the elements of MSG Sports&#8217; executive compensation program are reasonable and consistent with MSG Sports&#8217; objectives. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The MSG Sports independent compensation consultant collaborates with independent legal counsel and reports directly to MSG Sports&#8217;
Compensation Committee and, at the request of MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, the MSG Sports independent compensation consultant meets with members of management from time to time for the purpose of gathering information on management
proposals and recommendations to be presented to MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The services provided by the MSG Sports
independent compensation consultant to MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee during the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026 included: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee believes that the MSG Sports independent compensation consultant&#8217;s work did not raise any conflicts of interest during the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026. In reaching this conclusion, MSG

management&#8217;s recommendations on the compensation for MSG Sports&#8217; executive officers other than the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. Recommendations from MSG Sports&#8217; management are based on a comprehensive review and
analysis of the performance of MSG Sports and its business against <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> goals, strategies and metrics. Other members of MSG Sports&#8217; management provide support to MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation
Committee as needed. Based upon a review of performance and historical compensation, recommendations and information from members of MSG Sports&#8217; management, and recommendations and discussions with the MSG Sports independent compensation
consultant, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee determines and approves compensation for its executive officers. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>MSG Sports&#8217; Performance Objectives </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As described below under &#8220;&#8212; Elements of MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Program,&#8221; performance-based incentive compensation is
an important element of MSG Sports&#8217; executive compensation program. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports considers these performance objectives to be key
measures of MSG Sports&#8217; operating performance. As such, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee has incorporated AOI and revenues in MSG Sports&#8217; long-term incentive performance awards (i.e., performance stock units) and AOI in MSG
Sports&#8217; annual incentive awards. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports defines AOI, which is a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial
measure, as operating income (loss) excluding (i)&nbsp;depreciation, amortization and impairments of property and equipment, goodwill and other intangible assets, (ii)&nbsp;share-based compensation expense or benefit, (iii)&nbsp;restructuring
charges or credits, (iv)&nbsp;gains or losses on sales or dispositions of businesses, (v)&nbsp;the impact of purchase accounting adjustments related to business acquisitions, and (vi)&nbsp;gains and losses related to the remeasurement of liabilities
under the Madison Square Garden Sports Corp. Executive Deferred Compensation Plan (the &#8220;EDC Plan&#8221;). Because it is based upon operating income (loss), AOI (loss) also excludes interest expense (including cash interest expense) and other <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</FONT> income and expense items. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The performance measures used for purposes of annual incentives
or long-term awards may contemplate certain potential future adjustments and exclusions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Tally Sheets </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee has reviewed tally sheets prepared by the MSG Sports independent compensation consultant, setting
forth all components of compensation payable, and the benefits accruing, to MSG Sports&#8217; named executive officers for the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, including all cash compensation, benefits, perquisites and the current value of
outstanding equity-based awards. The tally sheets also set forth potential payouts to such named executive officers upon various termination scenarios. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Determining MSG Sports Compensation Levels; Benchmarking </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As part of the MSG Sports Compensation Committee&#8217;s review of total compensation for the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, the MSG
Sports independent compensation consultant assisted MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee in: (1)&nbsp;determining if a peer group should be used for comparative purposes, (2)&nbsp;assessing executive compensation in light of internal and
external considerations and (3)&nbsp;reviewing MSG Sports&#8217; equity and cash-based executive incentive programs, taking into account evolving market trends. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, in consultation with the MSG Sports
independent compensation consultant, considered market data (both industry-specific and general company data based on multiple broad-based compensation surveys) in order to appropriately assess compensation levels. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the fiscal year ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, in consultation with the MSG Sports independent
compensation consultant, determined not to utilize a peer group or specific target positioning in determining compensation given the limited number of comparable publicly-traded companies. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to the market data documented above, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee considered internal information (job responsibility,
experience, parity among executive officers, contractual commitments, attraction and retention of talent and historical compensation) to determine compensation. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; executive compensation philosophy is reflected in the principal elements of its executive compensation program, each of which
is important to MSG Sports&#8217; goal of attracting, retaining, motivating and </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Annual Cash Incentives </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Overview </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; annual cash incentives earned for performance in Fiscal Year 2026 were determined based on performance against goals
established by MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee under MSG Sports&#8217; Management Performance Incentive Plan (&#8220;MPIP&#8221;). MPIP is an annual incentive plan under which eligible members of MSG Sports&#8217; management, including the
NEOs, were provided an opportunity to earn an annual cash award. The initial funding level of the bonus pool was solely based on financial performance versus a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> AOI target for Fiscal Year 2026,
which initial funding level could be modified based on performance versus <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> and measurable key strategic objectives, resulting in a payout that falls within the range of 0% to 200% of target. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This annual incentive was designed to link executive compensation directly to MSG Sports&#8217; financial performance and performance on key
strategic initiatives by providing incentives and rewards based upon business performance during the applicable fiscal year. Mr. DiCicco was not eligible to participate in MSG Sports&#8217; Fiscal&nbsp;Year 2026 MPIP in accordance with the terms of
his employment agreement with MSG Sports. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As discussed in &#8220;Performance Targets&nbsp;&amp; Achievement Levels&#8221; below, as a
result of the level of achievement of the AOI target, the initial bonus funding level was 56.88% of target. MSG Sports incurred certain expenses that differed from the assumptions reflected in the budget approved by MSG Sports&#8217; board of
directors and used to establish the fiscal year 2026 AOI target, including an increase in revenue sharing expense, as well as an increase in team operations expenses driven by MSG Sports&#8217; continued investment in its teams. This investment
contributed to, among other things, the Knicks NBA Championship win in the 2025-26 NBA season. As a result, to better align the MPIP payout with actual company performance, based on recommendations from management, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation
Committee, in consultation with its independent advisors, approved adjustments to the calculated AOI result to account for the expenses discussed above. After giving effect to these adjustments, the final payout level of the annual cash incentives
based on financial performance was calculated at 100.00% of the target level. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, in consultation with its independent advisors and considering management&#8217;s recommendation, also reviewed MSG Sports&#8217;
performance against its pre-set goals, strategies and tactics for fiscal year 2026, and determined not to modify the adjusted financial score, resulting in a final MPIP payout of 100.00% of target for fiscal year 2026. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Target Award Opportunities </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Each employee
eligible for an annual incentive award from MSG Sports was assigned a target award equal to a percentage of that employee&#8217;s base salary as of the conclusion of the applicable fiscal year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Target annual incentive opportunities were based upon the applicable employee&#8217;s position, grade level, responsibilities and historical
and expected future contributions to MSG Sports. In addition, each employment agreement between MSG Sports and each of the NEOs contains a minimum target annual incentive award level. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee reviews the target
annual incentive award levels of the NEOs at least annually, subject to the minimum target annual incentive award level set forth in their employment agreements with MSG Sports. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, in its sole discretion and
subject to the terms of such employment agreements with MSG Sports, may revise target annual incentive award levels for the NEOs. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">110 </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Financial Component: </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the fiscal year
ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, the MPIP financial performance objective consisted of an AOI target from the budget approved by MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors. The initial MPIP funding pool was determined after assessing financial performance
against the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> AOI target, with the initial MPIP funding pool under this component ranging from 0 to 200% of target. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Based on the performance against the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> AOI target, the calculated result of the financial
component of the MPIP, giving effect to the payout provisions of the MPIP, was 56.88% of target. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The MPIP provides MSG Sports&#8217;
Compensation Committee with flexibility to make equitable adjustments to the structure and payouts that it deems appropriate to reflect the best interests of the business, including based on recommendations from management. Upon review of the
calculated result of the financial component of the MPIP, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee, considering recommendations from management and in consultation with its independent advisors, determined the calculated results should be adjusted
to account for certain items related to revenue sharing and team operations as discussed above. After reflecting such adjustments, the adjusted result of the financial component of the MPIP was 100.00% of the target level. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Strategic Modifier: </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the fiscal year
ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, the MPIP also included a strategic modifier component that could increase or decrease the initial <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AOI-funded</FONT> MPIP pool based on performance against relevant strategic goals, resulting
in a payout that falls within a range of 0% to 200% of target. These goals, and associated tactics and metrics, were reviewed and approved by MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee at the beginning of the year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Goal Setting Process:</I> In Fiscal Year 2026, numerous specific goals that were aligned with MSG Sports&#8217; broad strategic initiatives
were established for MSG Sports. Discrete tactics and metrics were enumerated to measure <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-end</FONT> achievement of these goals. Taking into account performance with respect to each goal and underlying strategies
and metrics, management could propose a modification to the initial <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AOI-funded</FONT> pool. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee would then assess management&#8217;s recommended modification relative to the level
of achievement against strategic goals and make an independent determination as to the appropriate modifier (if any). </P>

determined based on the extent to which goals, strategies and measurable metrics were achieved in the fiscal year. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Based on its review,
considering the recommendation of management, and in consultation with its independent advisors, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee determined not to further modify the financial score based on MSG Sports&#8217; strategic performance. As a

Compensation Committee seeks to ensure target goals are ambitious, requiring meaningful growth over the performance period, while threshold goals are expected to be achievable. Goals were set at the beginning of Fiscal Year 2026 based on MSG
Sports&#8217; long-range strategic plan, which is subject to review by MSG Sports&#8217; board of directors in connection with its approval of MSG Sports&#8217; annual budget. MSG Sports&#8217; long-range strategic plan is confidential, and
disclosure of those targets could provide information that could lead to competitive harm, and for this reason the performance stock unit financial performance targets are not disclosed. MSG Sports intends to disclose the revenues and AOI payout
results as a percentage of target as well as the resulting payout for the 2026 Performance Stock Units as a percentage of target measured in the last year of the performance period. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Fiscal Year 2024 Performance Stock Unit Awards </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The performance stock units granted by MSG Sports to its executive officers in the Fiscal Year 2024 (collectively, the &#8220;2024 Performance
Stock Units&#8221;) were subject to revenues and AOI performance objectives, which were each weighted at 50% over a performance period of July&nbsp;1, 2025 through June&nbsp;30, 2026 (the third year of the three-year performance award). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; financial performance against previously determined revenues and AOI as a percentage of target performance was calculated at
102.0% and 0.0%, respectively. Both revenues and AOI were impacted by amendments to MSG Sports&#8217; local telecast rights agreement with MSG Networks in Fiscal Year 2025, which was a result of MSG Networks debt restructuring process. The
amendments were not contemplated in the long-range plan underlying the 2024 Performance Stock Unit goals when they were established in Fiscal Year 2024. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In reviewing the 2024 Performance Stock Unit performance results, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee reviewed and considered the impact
of the MSG Networks amendments on revenues and AOI, including that the amendments were not contemplated when the performance goals were established and were undertaken in furtherance of MSG Sports&#8217; long-term interests. Based on recommendations
from management and in </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">114 </P>

</DIV></Center>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
consultation with its independent advisors, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee determined that the revenues and AOI results should be adjusted to exclude the impact of the amendments and
made an equitable adjustment to the performance results. After reflecting such adjustments, in August 2026, MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee certified performance against revenues and AOI at 104.8% and 90.1% of target, respectively, with a
resulting payout for the 2024 Performance Stock Units calculated at 97.4% of target. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee Policies Related to
Certain Compensation Matters </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The MSG Sports Compensation Committee&#8217;s charter sets forth certain provisions relating to the
consideration and granting of annual equity-based awards and other compensation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee is required to
establish a schedule for the consideration and granting of annual equity-based and other compensation, and the meeting to approve any annual equity-based awards and incentive compensation awards shall promptly follow the announcement of MSG
Sports&#8217; <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-end</FONT> earnings (except as MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee may otherwise agree). MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee also has the authority in its discretion to approve
equity-based awards at other times during the year for other reasons, including to provide compensation to new employees. MSG Sports&#8217; Compensation Committee does not take material <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-public</FONT> information
into account when determining the timing of the grant of equity-based awards, including options. The timing of MSG Sports&#8217; release of material <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-public</FONT> information is not based on affecting the value
of executive compensation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the MSG Sports Compensation Committee&#8217;s charter sets forth certain procedural matters
relating to the granting of stock options. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Insider Trading Policy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports has an insider trading policy that governs the purchase, sale and other disposition of its securities by MSG Sports itself and its
employees, directors and consultants. MSG Sports believes its insider trading policy is reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules and regulations and the exchange listing standards applicable to it. Among other
things, MSG Sports&#8217; insider trading policy prohibits its employees, directors and consultants from trading in its securities while in possession of material <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-public</FONT> information. The foregoing summary
of MSG Sports&#8217; insider trading policy does not purport to be complete and is qualified by reference to the full text of its insider trading policy, a copy of which can be found as an exhibit to its 2025 Form
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-K.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Hedging Policy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Insider Trading Policy prohibits all its directors, consultants and employees (including its executive officers), and all
members of their immediate families and any individual who is materially dependent upon them for financial support who resides in the same household, from directly or indirectly engaging in short sales, short sales against the box or other
&#8220;hedging&#8221; transactions unless otherwise permitted by MSG Sports. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Clawback Policy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">MSG Sports&#8217; Clawback Policy, which was established in accordance with the listing requirement of the NYSE, provides for the recovery or
&#8220;clawback&#8221; of certain erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation in the event that MSG Sports is required to prepare an accounting restatement. The policy was effective December&nbsp;1, 2023 and applies to incentive-based
compensation received by current and former executive officers of MSG Sports during the three fiscal years preceding an accounting restatement and after the effective date of the NYSE&#8217;s listing requirement, October&nbsp;2, 2023. </P>
